title: Cryogenics Engineer – Test Facility & Auxiliary Cryoplants
description: WHO WE ARE Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant. Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach. Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions. BY JOINING OUR TEAM YOU’LL GET TO Shape the architecture of the world’s first commercial fusion power plant – Own system-level decisions that determine how a first-of-a-kind energy technology is designed, integrated, and ultimately deployed at scale. Solve some of the most complex engineering challenges – Work across tightly coupled disciplines (plasma physics, magnets, cryogenics, manufacturing, controls, and more) to resolve critical trade-offs and turn cutting-edge science into a functioning product. Design real hardware with a pragmatic, fast-moving team from all over the world – Combine advanced simulation and systems thinking with a strong execution mindset, focusing on practical engineering solutions that accelerate the path to commercial fusion energy. YOUR IMPACT You will deliver the helium refrigerator and cryogenic distribution for Proxima's Alpha coil test facility, taking these systems from requirements and process design through procurement, installation and commissioning. You will also support the engineering of the refrigerator for the cryopumps of the neutral beam injectors and divertor, and act as the process and safety owner for these systems. WHAT YOU WILL DO Own the cryogenic supply infrastructure for the Alpha coil test facility, covering the main refrigerator, liquid nitrogen equipment, cryogenic distribution and interconnecting valve box, from concept to commissioning and test operation Define requirements, process flow diagrams and P&IDs for cryogenic refrigerators and ancillary systems such as helium storage tanks, LHe dewars, purification and gas recovery Size lines, valves and pressure relief devices based on your relief case definitions, in line with PED and relevant EN/ISO standards Write specifications and RFQ packages, evaluate offers, and act as expert customer for suppliers through design reviews, FAT, installation and site acceptance Plan and lead installation and commissioning, write operating procedures, and support operation on site close to Munich WHO YOU ARE A team player who loves challenges and is not afraid to experiment, take risks and learn from mistakes A proven track record of designing, building and commissioning cryogenic or similar gas systems in industrial plants, test facilities, accelerators, or space infrastructure Hands-on experience developing P&IDs, sizing pressure relief devices to recognised standards (e.g. ISO 21013, ISO 4126), and using process or system simulation tools such as EcosimPro or Aspen HYSYS for helium refrigeration plants or similar Experience with pressure equipment design to EN 13445 or AD 2000, and with CAD Proficiency with programming languages used in science and engineering (particularly Python) is highly beneficial but not essential Demonstrated ability to manage the delivery of complex systems with external suppliers to schedule and budget INTERVIEW PROCESS Recruiter Interview (30-60 min) Technical Screening (30 min) description: Company Description Experian is a global data and technology company, powering opportunities for people and businesses around the world. Job Description The Software Engineer (.NET/Azure) is a hands-on, mid-level contributor responsible for designing, building, and modernizing high-volume, high-transaction applications across the Experian Employer Services (EES) organization. You will write production code, participate in code reviews, evaluate SAST findings, and work closely with product, quality engineering, security, and operations partners to deliver secure, reliable software to our clients and partners. AI and automation are the main focus of our team. EES is adopting an AI-Driven Development Lifecycle (AI DLC) and spec-driven agentic development, in which teams define intent, constraints, acceptance criteria, and validation before AI agents build approved work. As an engineer in this model you will work from versioned specifications, direct AI coding agents to implement approved work, and oversee the review, testing, and security validation of what they produce. You will have already worked this way hands-on; this is a requirement of the role, not a learning goal. Humans remain accountable for technical decisions, data protection, and production outcomes. At Experian, we believe great work happens when people come together. We're focused on attracting talent in and around our designated hub locations who are open to collaborating with colleagues in person. Aligning employees to these talent markets helps foster collaboration, strengthen team connections, and support long-term career growth within Experian. This hybrid role reports to the Engineering Manager, Application Engineering, and reside in or near one of our collaboration hubs: Costa Mesa, CA; San Jose, CA; Allen, TX; Austin, TX; Franklin, TN; New York, NY; Schaumberg, IL; Washington, D.C.; Atlanta, GA; Boston, MA; Seattle, WA Responsibilities: Analyze new feature requirements with attention to design, software development best practices, testing strategy, database design, security, and cloud architecture, and turn them into clear, versioned specifications with explicit acceptance criteria that engineers and AI agents can verify. Build new and modernize existing .NET applications, APIs, and partner integrations, including responsive, accessible web UIs that work across devices.
